Table 2: Sensitivity analysis of the estimands: τ (top table) and η (bottom table) for N = 250 and K = 5 with ρ ∈ {0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9}. The true SP and FP estimands are reported along with the estimated sharp bounds. For each true ρ, the Bayesian results of posterior mean (P.M.) and coverage are computed for each assumed ρ, across 1, 000 treatment assignment mechanisms. Along the diagonal (dark grey cells), coverage is highest, as the true ρ coincides with the assumed ρ. The cells with coverage > 0.9 are shaded light grey to indicate cases where ρ misspecification gives satisfactory results.

Table 1: True estimands under the super population and finite population frameworks for different values of N and K, along with the nonparametric sharp bounds and the Bayesian finite population inference assuming known ρ = 0.7. Bayesian results are summarized over 1, 000 treatment assignment mechanisms.

Figure 1: Traceplots of β, α1 and α2 for the 3-category model with N = 100, 250 and 500 units based on five independent MCMC chains with different parameter initializations. Each column corresponds to the parameters for a specific N , while the rows display the changes in the estimated parameters with increasing N . The Gelman Rubin R̂ statistic is shown at the top right corner of each plot, recording the point estimate and 95% upper confidence limit. The black dashed lines indicate the true parameter values: β = −0.6 (in first row), α1 = −1 (in second row) and α2 = 0 (in third row).
